statutory_provisions: IPC s.304-B, s.113-B; Evidence Act s.113-8
aggravating_circumstances: Persistent demand for dowry, harassment, cruelty
neutral_facts: The accused, a married man, was convicted of causing the death of his wife, who committed suicide after being subjected to persistent harassment and cruelty from her husband and his brothers for not fulfilling their dowry demands. The victim's parents were not allowed to meet her for several months prior to her death. The victim consumed a pesticide, which was confirmed through a postmortem examination. The prosecution presented evidence from multiple witnesses, including the victim's mother and father, who testified about the ongoing harassment and demands for dowry. The trial court convicted the accused under Sections 498A and 304-B of the IPC, while acquitting his two brothers. The High Court affirmed the conviction under Section 304-B, citing the persistent cruelty and harassment as the proximate cause of the victim's death.
